statements.attributed: The field has grown to include intermetallic and ceramic compounds, as well as microstructures with any number and any type of these phases.
statements.quote: Initially emphasizing single-phase, solid solution metallic alloys, the field has grown to include intermetallic and ceramic compounds, as well as microstructures with any number and any type of these phases.

statements.attributed: HEAs were originally defined as a blend of 5 or more elements with concentrations between 5 and 35 atom percent.
statements.numbers: 5 or more elements, 5 to 35 atom percent
statements.quote: HEAs were originally defined as a blend of 5 or more elements with concentrations between 5 and 35 atom percent, but the field now includes materials with as few as 3 principal elements, and where the maximum element concentration may be higher than 35 atom percent.

statements.attributed: Each HEA can be modified by minor elemental additions as for current element-based alloys.
statements.quote: Each HEA is a new alloy base, since each HEA can be modified by minor elemental additions as for current element-based alloys.

statements.attributed: A 5-component system will have 906 different CCA bases if every 10% change in composition gives a distinct CCA base.
statements.quote: For example, if every 10% change in composition gives a distinct CCA base, then a 5-component system will have 906 different CCA bases.

statements.attributed: Many elements can be substituted on a single sublattice, and a host structure can be retained even when adding elements that form different crystal structures.
statements.quote: However, HEA studies show that many elements can be substituted on a single sublattice, and that a host structure can be retained even when adding elements that form different crystal structures.

statements.attributed: HEA concepts can significantly expand conventional alloying approaches for functional materials.
statements.quote: With more principal elements than sublattices, HEA concepts can significantly expand conventional alloying approaches for functional materials.
